summary: HTTP order intake with durable acceptance (202 + order ID only after commit), a transactional outbox to a Service Bus queue, and an idempotent ERP worker. During ERP outages the worker pauses consumption; per-message retries are new messages scheduled before the original is completed; a sweeper re-publishes any order stuck beyond the outage budget. Draft: blocking questions on ERP idempotency, validation rules and data classification remain. Nothing deployed.

requirements.title: Accept customer orders through an HTTP REST API
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: POST /orders returns 202 with an order ID only after the order row and outbox row are committed in one transaction; returns 4xx for invalid requests

requirements.title: Handle approximately 20,000 orders per day
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Load test sustains 20,000 synthetic orders in 24 hours with zero lost orders; peak-rate test pending REQ-008

requirements.title: Tolerate ERP unavailability of up to 45 minutes
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: During a simulated 60-minute ERP outage, intake keeps returning 202, zero messages reach the DLQ for ERP-unavailable reasons, and backlog drains after recovery

requirements.title: Accepted orders must not disappear
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Every order with a 202 response ends in exactly one terminal state (ERP-confirmed, rejected-with-reason, or manual-review) verified by a daily reconciliation count with zero unexplained gaps

requirements.title: Prevent duplicate business processing in the ERP
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Resubmitting the same client idempotency key returns the original order ID; redelivering the same message produces at most one ERP order, verified by ERP external reference lookup

requirements.title: Validate orders before ERP delivery
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Requests failing schema or business rules receive 400/422 with error detail and are never written to the outbox; business rule set supplied by QUE-003

requirements.title: Use Azure as the integration platform
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Architecture review confirms every runtime component is an Azure-managed service or justified exception

requirements.title: Peak order rate and burst profile
End-to-end processing latency target (accepted to ERP-confirmed)
Data classification and residency of order data
Callers authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID OAuth 2.0 client credentials
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: Requests without a valid token for the API audience receive 401 at APIM

requirements.title: Callers can query order status
requirements.source: Assumption: needed because 202 means accepted, not completed
requirements.acceptanceCriteria: GET /orders/{id} returns current state within 1 second for an existing order

components.title: API gateway
components.sku: Standard v2 (assumed; Premium v2 if full VNet injection required)
components.responsibility: validate-jwt, rate limiting, request size limits, correlation ID injection, routing to intake

components.title: Order intake API
components.azureService: Azure Functions (Flex Consumption or Premium plan)
components.responsibility: Validate request, insert-if-absent on idempotency key, write order + outbox row in one transaction, return 202 or the original result

components.title: Order state store with outbox table
components.responsibility: Source of truth for order state; unique constraint on idempotency key; outbox rows; monotonic state transitions guarded by version column

components.title: Outbox relay
components.responsibility: Publish unsent outbox rows with MessageId = order ID (first publish only) and OrderId property; mark rows sent; safe to re-run

components.title: Order queue
components.sku: Standard (assumed; Premium if private endpoints or geo-replication required)
components.responsibility: Durable buffer between intake and ERP; DLQ for poison messages; duplicate detection as a send-side optimisation only

components.title: ERP delivery worker
components.responsibility: Idempotent ERP call keyed on the OrderId property (ERP external reference); circuit breaker that pauses receiving during ERP outages; per-message retries scheduled as NEW messages (MessageId = {orderId}:retry:{n}) before completing the original; reconcile uncertain outcomes

components.title: Secrets and certificates
components.responsibility: ERP credentials if ERP lacks Entra ID; accessed by managed identity only

components.title: Observability
components.azureService: Application Insights + Log Analytics + Azure Monitor alerts
components.responsibility: Distributed tracing via correlation ID, backlog and DLQ metrics, reconciliation dashboards

components.title: Reconciliation sweeper
components.responsibility: Find orders in a non-terminal state older than the outage budget plus margin and re-publish them with MessageId = {orderId}:sweep:{runId}; the state store, not the broker, is the source of truth

decisions.title: Asynchronous acceptance with 202 instead of synchronous ERP call
decisions.rationale: ERP can be down for 45 minutes; a synchronous call would fail or time out for the whole outage
decisions.tradeoff: 202 means accepted, not completed; callers need status query or callback (REQ-013)

decisions.title: Transactional outbox instead of direct publish from intake
decisions.rationale: Removes the gap where the DB commit succeeds but the Service Bus send fails (or the reverse)
decisions.alternative: Send to Service Bus then write DB, or write DB then send
decisions.tradeoff: Extra relay component and outbox housekeeping; small added delay

decisions.title: Service Bus queue instead of Event Grid for order delivery
decisions.rationale: Point-to-point command with competing consumer, pull-based consumption, DLQ, sessions available if ordering becomes a requirement
decisions.alternative: Event Grid push delivery (retries up to 24 h, no ordering guarantee)
decisions.tradeoff: Consumer owns retry pacing; Standard tier lacks private endpoints

decisions.title: Azure Functions instead of Logic Apps for intake and worker
decisions.rationale: Transactional insert-if-absent and outbox logic are clearer and testable in code
decisions.alternative: Logic Apps Standard (attractive if an SAP/ERP connector replaces custom client code)
decisions.tradeoff: More code to own; revisit if the ERP is SAP and the managed connector fits

decisions.title: End-to-end idempotency in the application; Service Bus duplicate detection is not relied upon
decisions.rationale: Duplicate detection only drops repeat MessageIds inside its time window (default 10 minutes, max 7 days) and does not cover consumer redelivery or ERP-side uncertainty. Retries and DLQ replays therefore use their own MessageIds; business idempotency keys on the OrderId property
decisions.tradeoff: Requires ERP external-reference support or a lookup before create (RSK-001)

decisions.title: Pause consumption during outages; retry individual messages with a new MessageId; reconcile from the state store
decisions.rationale: Abandoning burns maxDeliveryCount (default 10) within minutes. Re-sending with the original MessageId is unsafe: duplicate detection also applies to scheduled messages, so a retry inside the window is silently dropped, and completing before scheduling loses the order on a crash
decisions.alternative: Rejected: abandon and let the broker retry (dead-letters healthy orders within minutes). Rejected: complete, then reschedule reusing the original MessageId (silently dropped by duplicate detection; lost on a crash)
decisions.tradeoff: More worker logic (breaker, retry identity, schedule-then-complete) and a sweeper job to build and test

testCases.title: Acknowledgement only after commit
testCases.expectedResult: Fault injected after commit but before response: retry with same key returns original order ID; fault before commit: no row, no 202

testCases.title: Concurrent duplicate submissions
testCases.expectedResult: 50 parallel POSTs with one idempotency key create one order and one outbox row

testCases.title: ERP outage of 60 minutes
testCases.expectedResult: Intake stays available, DLQ count stays 0, backlog drains after recovery, all orders reach a terminal state

testCases.title: Relay crash mid-batch
testCases.expectedResult: Every committed outbox row is published at least once after restart

testCases.title: ERP timeout with unknown outcome
testCases.expectedResult: Worker looks up ERP by external reference before retrying; at most one ERP order exists

testCases.title: Missing or invalid token
testCases.expectedResult: 401 at APIM; intake function not invoked

testCases.title: Daily volume load test
testCases.expectedResult: 20,000 orders in 24 hours, zero lost, reconciliation clean

testCases.title: Poison message
testCases.expectedResult: Message failing deterministically goes to DLQ, order marked manual-review, alert raised, resubmission tool restores it after fix

testCases.title: Architecture conformance review
testCases.expectedResult: Reviewer confirms all runtime components are Azure services

testCases.title: Lost acknowledgement to caller
testCases.expectedResult: Client times out after commit, retries with same idempotency key and receives the original order ID; one order row exists

testCases.title: Worker crash between scheduling a retry and completing the original
testCases.expectedResult: Original is redelivered and a duplicate retry may exist; at most one ERP order exists for the OrderId (verified by external-reference lookup) and the order reaches a terminal state

testCases.title: Complete fails after a successful ERP call
testCases.expectedResult: Redelivered message finds the order already confirmed (lookup by OrderId) and completes without a second ERP call

testCases.title: Retry sent while duplicate detection is enabled
testCases.expectedResult: Retry message (MessageId {orderId}:retry:n) is delivered, not dropped, within the duplicate-detection window

testCases.title: Circuit breaker open for 60 minutes
testCases.expectedResult: No message reaches the DLQ for ERP-unavailable reasons; delivery counts stay within budget; processing resumes when the probe succeeds

testCases.title: Stuck order recovered by sweeper
testCases.expectedResult: An order whose message was deleted manually is re-published by the sweeper and reaches a terminal state

testCases.title: DLQ resubmission inside the duplicate-detection window
testCases.expectedResult: Replayed message ({orderId}:replay:{seq}) is delivered and processed once

risks.title: ERP idempotency contract unknown
risks.mitigation: Confirm external-reference uniqueness or lookup API before build; otherwise add a pre-create lookup and manual reconciliation

risks.title: Retry design can dead-letter or silently drop orders
risks.mitigation: Pause consumption on ERP outage; per-message retries as new messages ({orderId}:retry:{n}) scheduled before the original is completed; never reuse the original MessageId; sweeper re-publishes stuck orders
risks.evidence: Microsoft docs: abandon increments delivery count (default max 10); scheduled messages are included in duplicate detection

risks.title: Standard tier lacks private networking
risks.mitigation: If classification requires private endpoints, move Service Bus to Premium and re-price
risks.evidence: Microsoft Learn: private endpoints are Premium-only

risks.title: Outbox relay becomes a silent single point of delay
risks.mitigation: Alert on oldest unsent outbox row age
